# Universal Enterprise Engineering Kit

## Product positioning

A reusable GitHub repository governance and AI-assisted engineering framework for teams building software across multiple languages, platforms, and business domains.

## What it includes

- Repository-wide AI engineering playbook with discovery, security, testing, operations, and approval boundaries.
- Nine specialist AI agent profiles for architecture, security, quality, dependencies, data, APIs, AI safety, performance, and releases.
- Path-aware standards for frontend, backend, APIs, databases, infrastructure, mobile, AI, data/ML, testing, and common language ecosystems.
- Reusable prompts for repository audits, safe implementation, threat modeling, dependency audits, incident response, and release readiness.
- Operational runbooks for incident response, security incidents, migrations, backup/restore, releases, and AI safety.
- Configurable project CI runner, JSON project profile, GitHub configuration validation, contribution templates, and Dependabot ecosystem examples.
- Optional profile directory for domain- or organization-specific policies, kept separate from the universal core.

## Who it is for

Independent developers, software agencies, product teams, startups, platform engineering teams, and organizations that want a consistent engineering baseline across repositories.

## What makes it useful

It gives teams a clear starting point and reusable governance patterns without imposing one framework or cloud provider. Project commands, environments, security settings, workflows, and release controls remain explicit and configurable.

## Honest scope

The kit is not a hosted CI service, application framework, security certification, legal license, or guarantee of enterprise readiness. It does not automatically configure GitHub organization settings, provision infrastructure, or validate every stack. Buyers must adapt their project profile and verify controls in their own environment.

## Customization / services

Potential commercial editions can add organization-specific policy, validated workflows for selected technology stacks, branded documentation, migration support, training, and managed update cadence. Do not advertise features until implemented, tested, and supported.
